# Phase 7: Getting in the door — networking, sequencing, negotiation

*from week 1, in parallel* · [Track on the site](https://arubad.github.io/AI_Research_Journey/#p7)

One referral is worth roughly forty cold applications (cold applications reply at ~1–2%, referrals at ~20%+), so the pipeline is built months before you need it, in parallel with everything above.

## Build the referral pipeline (from week 1)
- Be visible at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP — talk to people, don't just attend. Workshops and poster sessions are easier entry points for a student.
- Collaborate across institutions; co-authors become referrers. Open-source contributions to repos labs actually use (vLLM, TRL, nanoGPT forks, CS336 leaderboards) are the student equivalent.
- Reach out informally months before searching: nobody refers a stranger. Reconnecting with people you haven't spoken to in years is normal and expected.
- Ask advisors, classmates and collaborators who already moved to industry. Use friends and recruiters to learn which teams actually have headcount; that can matter more than your preparation.

## Sequence the applications
1. Apply to less-desired companies first; they are practice, not consolation prizes. Watch your stamina — do not burn out before the companies you care about.
1. Do not open your top-choice processes until you hold at least one offer; leverage multiplies.
1. Time processes so offers land close together. Deadlines are flexible and recruiters expect you to finish other processes, but investigate each company's reputation for "exploding" offers.
1. Customize prep per company: recent papers, research agenda, product. Each interview is a slightly different class with three days to cram, so keep per-topic notes you can swap in.

**Negotiate.** The work is not done at the offer. Initial offers leave room by design and recruiters will say so. Before every recruiter call, write down what you will and will not share and a few lines you can say verbatim; anticipate their questions. Lean on friends for market data points. A few weeks of effort here can equal years of pay difference at the initial number.

## Keep this private
Contacts, applications, offers and negotiation notes should not live in a public repo. `private/` in this folder is git-ignored; use it for local notes only.
